question: Which of the following is NOT a phase transition between the states of matter?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Emission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Emission** is not a phase transition; it refers to the release of energy, often in the form of light or radiation, from a source.
 
• Phase transitions involve changes in the state of matter, such as from solid to liquid or liquid to gas.
 
• Examples of phase transitions include sublimation, condensation, and vaporization, all of which involve changing physical states.
 
• Emission, on the other hand, is more commonly associated with physical processes like the emission of photons or particles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation:**

 
 
• Sublimation is the phase transition from a solid directly to a gas, bypassing the liquid state.
 
• An example of sublimation is dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) turning directly into carbon dioxide gas.
 
 
 
• **Condensation:**
 
 
• Condensation is the phase transition from gas to liquid.
 
• This process is commonly observed when water vapor in the air condenses to form dew on cool surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Vaporization:**
 
 
• Vaporization is the phase transition from liquid to gas.
 
• Boiling water turning into steam is a typical example of vaporization.
 
 
 
• **Deposition:**
 
 
• Deposition is the phase transition from a gas directly to a solid, skipping the liquid phase.
 
• Frost formation from water vapor is an example of deposition.
